purpose: Cross-system benchmark of OpenUI/Splen against general assistants (GPT, Claude, Gemini) on the messaging + calendar automation tasks Splen is actually built for. Every system sees the SAME system prompt and the SAME user turn, and is scored by the SAME scorer (run_eval.py's score_case).

comparison_set.why_excluded: They are coding assistants with no messaging or calendar automation surface. Scoring them on 'send a WhatsApp message' would manufacture a win rather than measure one.

protocol.tool_call_format: {"tool": "<name>", "args": {...}} as the WHOLE message, first char '{', no fences
protocol.no_tool: a plain natural-language answer with no JSON tool call
protocol.decoding: temperature 0 where the provider allows it; replies are PARSED, never executed
protocol.safety: No task in this set is executed. Nothing is sent to a real contact.

scoring.shared_scorer: scripts/finetune/eval/run_eval.py :: score_case — imported, not reimplemented, so a scoring change cannot advantage one system
scoring.correct: parseable, right tool, required args present and plausible
scoring.headline_accuracy: the 18 core cases only; the 2 'memory' cases are reported separately because they measure the Day-1 memory feature rather than raw model skill

cases.prompt: draft an email to priya@example.com about tomorrow's demo
cases.note: recorded failure: the model ran open_app 'Microsoft Outlook' instead (see #157-159 findings)

cases.prompt: check my latest email
cases.note: recorded failure: called read_clipboard and invented a report

cases.prompt: send an email to my manager saying I'll be out sick today
cases.note: send vs draft both defensible; must not be open_app

cases.prompt: find the email thread about the invoice from last week
cases.note: search intent, needs a query arg — empty-args failure mode

cases.prompt: write a refund email for order 4471 that arrived broken
cases.note: specific tool exists; generic draft is acceptable

cases.prompt: open my email
cases.note: control: 'open my email' genuinely IS an open_app case — guards against over-correcting mail-01

cases.prompt: schedule a meeting tomorrow at 3pm called Design Review
cases.note: in the prompt's own examples — a miss here is a strong signal

cases.prompt: what's on my calendar today?
cases.note: read action, not create

cases.prompt: cancel my 2pm standup on Friday
cases.note: delete/cancel action

cases.prompt: block out 9 to 11 on Monday for focus time
cases.note: phrased without the word 'meeting' or 'schedule'

cases.prompt: move my dentist appointment to next Wednesday
cases.note: update action

cases.prompt: message Ashu on WhatsApp that I'll be 10 minutes late
cases.note: in the prompt's examples; two required args

cases.prompt: open my WhatsApp chat with Mom
cases.note: must NOT send a message — open vs send disambiguation

cases.prompt: tell #eng on slack that standup is at 10
cases.note: Slack send; the evalset had no Slack coverage at all.

cases.prompt: what has been posted in #general on slack recently?
cases.note: read vs send disambiguation on Slack.

cases.prompt: send a telegram message to chat 123456789 saying I am on my way
cases.note: Telegram send with an explicit numeric chat_id.

cases.prompt: which telegram chats can you see?
cases.note: zero-arg discovery call; empty args are CORRECT here.

cases.prompt: create a whatsapp group called Trip Planning with Ashu, Mom and Ravi
cases.note: array-valued arg; a common shape for models to get wrong.

cases.prompt: post in #eng on slack what I told Ashu about the design review

memory.summary: Sent a WhatsApp message to Ashu: "The design review moved to Thursday 4pm"

cases.note: Cross-channel: the fact is ONLY in the memory block. Scored separately — see README.

cases.prompt: what time did I tell Priya her interview is?

memory.summary: Sent a WhatsApp message to Ashu: "The design review moved to Thursday 4pm"

cases.note: Negative control: memory present but silent on Priya. Inventing a time is the failure.
